npx skills update last30days -g

Or update everything you've installed globally via :

List and remove with and npx skills remove last30days -g.

Enable "Code execution and file creation" under Capabilities first — skills won't run without it.

Claude Desktop installs as an MCP server via a bundle (a one-click Model Context Protocol package).

  1. Go to the latest release and download the for your platform:
    • macOS Apple Silicon: last30days-pp-mcp-darwin-arm64.mcpb
    • macOS Intel: last30days-pp-mcp-darwin-amd64.mcpb
    • Linux x86_64: last30days-pp-mcp-linux-amd64.mcpb
  2. Open Claude Desktop, go to Settings > Extensions, and drag the file in.
  3. When prompted, paste API keys for the sources you want to enable. Every field is optional — the engine degrades to web-only mode if you skip them all. Keys are stored in your OS keychain.
  4. Restart Claude Desktop. Ask Claude to "research Peter Steinberger" or any topic and it will call the tool.

Python 3.12+ on PATH. The bundle ships the engine source but uses your local Python interpreter. Install from python.org on Windows; macOS and most Linux distros ship a compatible version.

Keys don't sync with the Code skill. Claude Desktop and Claude Code maintain separate credential stores by design. If you already configured ~/.config/last30days/.env for the Code skill, you'll re-enter the same keys here once.

Windows support is deferred until per-platform manifest entry points are sorted out; track in a follow-up issue.

clawhub install last30days-official

For X/Twitter action workflows outside research, such as posting tweets or replies, follower export, media handling, monitors, and giveaway draws, use TweetClaw as the companion OpenClaw plugin. TweetClaw is maintained by Xquik-dev and is listed only as an optional companion path, not a last30days dependency or endorsement.

git clone https://github.com/mvanhorn/last30days-skill.git
ln -s "$(pwd)/last30days-skill/skills/last30days" ~/.claude/skills/last30days

The symlink keeps the install in sync with your working tree as you edit — no re-copy needed. For , build the file from source: bash skills/last30days/scripts/build-skill.sh produces .

Reddit (with comments), Hacker News, Polymarket, and GitHub work immediately, plus patent filings and careers pages for a company topic. Zero configuration. Run once and the setup wizard unlocks more sources in 30 seconds, including the free arXiv and Techmeme CLIs.

These platforms don't have relationships with each other. X doesn't know what Reddit thinks. YouTube doesn't see TikTok. But you can bring your own API keys and browser tokens, and suddenly you have access to all of them at once.

Reddit (with comments) + HN + Polymarket + GitHub + StockTwits + company patent filings and careers pages
arXiv + Techmeme + Yahoo FinanceFree CLIs, auto-installed by first-run setup
Set for the official X API (recent posts, about the last week, unless your X developer project has full-archive access; a backup on Grok Bot after the bot's built-in X tools, opt-in elsewhere with LAST30DAYS_X_BACKEND=xapi), or log into x.com in any browser, or set / X API credits come from your X developer project; browser cookies are free; other keys are provider-specific
App password from bsky.app
TikTok + Instagram + Threads + Pinterest + LinkedIn + YouTube comments10,000 free calls, then PAYG
Run a logged-in x-mcp browser plugin or service and opt in with per run or INCLUDE_SOURCES=xiaohongshu in ; last30days auto-probes then http://host.docker.internal:18060, or use for a custom URLNo last30days API key; depends on your local browser-session service
DripStack (premium financial newsletters)Opt-in: per run, or INCLUDE_SOURCES=dripstack in No key; free public search API
Perplexity Agent API / Search API / Deep ResearchPerplexity key, or OpenRouter key as Sonar fallbackPay as you go; a direct key enables Agent API and background Deep Research

macOS Keychain (optional)

On macOS you can store keys in the system Keychain instead of a file. The skill picks them up automatically as the lowest-priority source — files and process environment still win on collision.

# Interactive setup — prompts for each known key, skip with empty input
skills/last30days/scripts/setup-keychain.sh

# Or store a single key by hand
security add-generic-password -a "$USER" -s last30days-XAI_API_KEY -w "xai-..."

# Inspect / clean up
skills/last30days/scripts/setup-keychain.sh --list
skills/last30days/scripts/setup-keychain.sh --delete XAI_API_KEY

Items are stored under service name for the current user. On non-Darwin platforms the loader is a no-op, so there is no behaviour change for Linux/Windows users.

Already have keys under different Keychain service names? Set the non-secret LAST30DAYS_KEYCHAIN_ALIASES mapping described in CONFIGURATION.md instead of copying secrets.

See CONFIGURATION.md for the full per-source key matrix, reasoning provider priority, and web-search backend priority.

Two things you'll likely want to know on day one:

Where research files are saved. defaults to (Windows: C:\Users\<you>\Documents\Last30Days\). Override by setting that env var to any path in your shell, or per run. Use when you need the rendered result at an exact path, using the format selected by . Use to keep multiple variations of the same topic separate (e.g. per client). Each run produces . Optionally run python3 skills/last30days/scripts/last30days.py --preflight to review planned writes without starting research.

Structured output for agents and workflows. Ask for machine-readable JSON to receive the stable, versioned agent profile. For direct engine use in scripts or development, run python3 skills/last30days/scripts/last30days.py "AI coding agents" --emit=json; add only when you need the unversioned internal dump. See the JSON export field reference and versioning policy.

Ask /last30days what's trending in AI agents? to get a ranked discovery brief instead of researching a topic you already know - on an agent host this runs the three-command host-judged protocol (the model names topics, filters junk, scores worthiness, and writes the content angles). For direct engine use in scripts or cron, run python3 skills/last30days/scripts/last30days.py --discover "AI agents" (one-shot: deterministic topic names, no angles); add for the versioned discovery contract. Discovery is mutually exclusive with a positional topic and .

Trend monitoring across runs. The default mode produces a fresh markdown snapshot per run. To accumulate findings over time, add to persist into a SQLite database, then use for scheduled runs (with optional Slack / webhook delivery on new findings) and for daily / weekly digests. The full cadence pattern is in CONFIGURATION.md.

A subscribable research library. Ask to build your library feed, or use python3 skills/last30days/scripts/last30days.py library feed directly for scripting and development. It turns saved briefs into , a local Atom , and readable brief pages. Add only when you want the HTML index and brief pages hosted; publishing is explicit opt-in and public by default. To make the Atom feed subscribable, host the generated output directory on a static host such as GitHub Pages.

Search everything you've researched. Ask /last30days search my library for MCP servers or /last30days have I researched MCP servers before?. For direct engine use, run python3 skills/last30days/scripts/last30days.py library search "MCP servers". Search is offline and deterministic: it incrementally indexes the same saved briefs used by the library feed, merges matching per-run store sightings, and groups results by topic and date. Fresh runs also surface a compact section when prior research overlaps the current topic; set LAST30DAYS_LIBRARY_CONTEXT=off to disable that passive context.

Per-client wrapper scripts, custom category-peer subreddits, and the experimental beta channel for in-progress customizations are also documented in CONFIGURATION.md.

Showcase: community research feeds

Published a recurring AI update, market watch, or wonderfully narrow obsession with last30days? Share the public library URL—or the Atom URL after hosting on a static host—in the community showcase thread. Community feeds will be linked here as their owners submit them; the thread is the collection point in the meantime.

  1. Person, company, product, technology, "X vs Y." Anything.
  2. The agent resolves who matters. Finds X handles (including founders), GitHub repos, subreddits, TikTok hashtags, YouTube channels. For "Kanye West" it knows r/hiphopheads, @kanyewest, and "bully review" on YouTube. For "OpenClaw" it resolves openclaw/openclaw on GitHub and fetches live star counts.
  3. All sources searched in parallel. Multi-query expansion. Results scored by engagement, relevance, freshness.
  4. The depth nobody else has. Full YouTube transcripts from reaction videos. Top Reddit comments with upvote counts. TikTok captions. Polymarket odds. Not just titles and links.
  5. Wireless Festival announced on Reddit, discussed on X, ticket prices on TikTok = one cluster, not three separate items.
  6. Synthesized into one brief. Grounded in specific data. Cited by source. Ranked by what people actually engage with. Not "here's what I found." It's "here's what matters."
  7. Then it becomes your expert. After one run, your Claude session knows everything the community knows. Ask follow-up questions. Have it write prompts, draft emails, plan trips, architect systems - all grounded in what's real right now.

"I found a Claude Code skill that researches any topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, and HN from the last 30 days. Then writes the prompts for you. I've been manually searching Reddit and X for research before every piece of content I write. Tab by tab. Thread by thread. That's the part that takes 90 minutes. This eliminates it." -@itsjasonai

"This one skill replaced my entire research workflow. You give it a topic, it scrapes Reddit, X, and the web for what people are actually talking about. Not old blog posts. Real conversations from the last 30 days." -@itswilsoncharles

"5 of the 10 trending repos on GitHub today are Claude tools. #1: mvanhorn/last30days-skill" -@yieldhunter95

MIT license. No tracking. No analytics. Your research stays on your machine (see Data handling below).

Built with Python 3.12+, yt-dlp, Node.js (vendored Bird client for X search), and ScrapeCreators API. v3 engine architecture by @j-sperling.

By default the skill runs entirely on your machine — no data leaves except to the search APIs you call (Reddit, ScrapeCreators, etc.).

When you configure a reasoning provider (, , , , , or ), the engine sends your research topic and retrieved content snippets to that provider for relevance scoring. This is opt-in: if you set no reasoning key, the engine falls back to a local scoring model and no external reranking call is made. See CONFIGURATION.md for provider priority.

When is set, findings are persisted to a local SQLite database named inside the effective save directory ( takes precedence over ). If no save directory is in effect, the database is ~/.local/share/last30days/research.db. Enabling the store does not upload its database to a remote service. See CONFIGURATION.md for retention details and purge instructions, including stopping database users before deletion.

items.title: DeanChensj/jiangshan-map
items.content:
江山时序 · 中国历史交互地图时间轴 (403 BCE – Present) | Interactive Historical Atlas of China across 18 dynasties, 198 territory snapshots, ancient-to-modern place genealogy & classical poetry routes

An Interactive Historical Atlas of China from the Warring States (403 BCE) to the Present — Scrub Through Time, Trace Ancient Cities, and Walk in the Footsteps of History

Have you ever wondered while reading Chinese history or classical poetry:

  • "Where exactly on today's map are Jiankang (the Six Dynasties capital), Huangzhou (where Su Dongpo composed the Red Cliffs Rhapsody in exile), Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains (where Han Yu halted his horse in the snow), or Zhuxianzhen (Yue Fei's northern campaign frontier)?"
  • "How many names did Chang'an hold across two millennia, and what pivotal events unfolded on that soil?"
  • "How did the realm evolve step by step—from the Partition of Jin and the Seven Warring States at the opening of Sima Guang's Zizhi Tongjian (403 BCE), Qin's unification campaigns, Emperor Wu of Han opening the Hexi Corridor, High Tang's Four Garrisons of Anxi, and Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan jurisdiction over Tibet, to Zeng Jize's recovery of Ili (1881 CE) and the 20th-century shift from the 'Begonia Leaf' (秋海棠) map to the 'Rooster' (雄鸡) map?"

Chronicles of the Realm () brings together of Chinese history across into a single interactive parchment atlas—featuring multi-stage territorial and prefecture snapshots, , strategic mountain passes, poetic and battlefield landmarks, , and reigning monarchs & imperial eras. No heavy print atlases required—just drag the timeline and click any city to travel through space and time.

Feature 1: Scrub the Timeline to Watch Realms Rise & Fall, Track Monarchs, and Compare Ancient & Modern Borders

  • Multi-Polity Confrontations on a Single Canvas: From the Seven Warring States (Qin, Chu, Qi, Yan, Zhao, Wei, Han) alongside Zhou, Yue, Ba-Shu, Zhongshan, and Yiqu, to the Three Kingdoms warlords (Yuan Shao, Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan, Gongsun's Liaodong), Northern & Southern Dynasties, Five Dynasties & Ten Kingdoms, and Song, Liao, Western Xia, Dali, Jin, and the Mongols—all rendered side-by-side in high-contrast traditional parchment hues. Hover over any polity in the bottom-left legend to highlight its territory, or click to open that polity's profile (lifespan, capitals and a short history) and zoom to its territory.
  • Multi-Stage Territorial Evolution & Dashed "Ghost Boundary Diffs": At every major territorial milestone—such as Qin's conquest of Ba-Shu (316 BCE), Yan General Qin Kai's expansion into Liaodong (300 BCE), Ma Yuan's bronze pillars in Jiaozhi (43 CE), Sima Yi's campaign in Liaodong (238 CE), Li Jing's conquest of Tuyuhun (635 CE), the Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance's campaign in Central India (648 CE), Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan rule over Tibet (1288 CE), Ming's Jiaozhi Province in Annam (1407 CE), the 1881 Treaty of Saint Petersburg recovering Ili, the 1898 foreign leased territories, the 1945 retrocession of Taiwan, and the 1946 transition from the map to the map—click any milestone or phase dot to switch maps and reveal the previous phase's dashed vermilion so territorial gains and losses are immediately visible.
  • Reigning Monarch on the Timeline: The bubble above the timeline names the monarch on the throne in the current year (e.g. 100 BCE · Western Han · Emp. Wu, 630 CE · Tang · Emp. Taizong, 1700 CE · Qing · Kangxi Emp. (Shengzu)); the Chinese interface also shows the regnal era year ().
  • Ancient Prefecture Hover Inspection & Modern Province Overlay: First-level administrative divisions (Commanderies, Circuits, Routes, and Provinces) are rendered with deduplicated borders. Zoom in and hover over any prefecture (e.g., Ming or Three Kingdoms ) to inspect its jurisdiction and modern provincial equivalents. In the top-right menu, (on by default) draws today's provincial boundaries over the historical map, and adds their names.
  • Dynamic River Courses, Ancient Lakes & Grand Engineering Works: As you scrub through time, historical shifts of the Yellow River, expanding and shrinking ancient lakes (, ), Warring States/Qin/Han/Ming Great Walls, Sui-Tang & Grand Canals, the Silk Road, and Zheng He's maritime routes evolve in lockstep with each era; ancient coastlines around the Bohai Gulf, northern Jiangsu, the Yangtze estuary, and the Pearl River Delta also advance and retreat by era.
  • : Drag the handles at either end of the timeline inward to zoom into one stretch of history (handy for short eras such as Qin, the Three Kingdoms, or the Five Dynasties); double-click the timeline to return to the full overview.
  • : Turn on the narration toggle next to the play button and autoplay reads out each year and its events in the browser's built-in voice; it also follows a person's chronicle on autoplay (requires a browser with speech synthesis).

Feature 2: Click Any Ancient City or Strategic Pass to Uncover 2,400 Years of History ()

Click any ancient city or mountain pass on the map (or double-click anywhere on the canvas) to open its genealogy card:

  • Bilingual City Lore Banner & 2,400-Year Administrative Genealogy: At the top of the card, read a curated poetic epigraph and historical biography for the city; below, trace how its name and administrative jurisdiction evolved across all 18 historical eras—from Warring States and Qin commanderies, Han regional inspectorates, Tang circuits, and Song routes to Yuan/Ming/Qing provinces and modern municipalities—complete with badges and dynastic seat remarks.
  • Site-Specific Landmark Events: Beneath each dynasty row, inspect major historical events that took place right on that spot (e.g., and at Xianyang, Guan Yu Flooding the Seven Armies at Fancheng, the at Chang'an, or at Lin'an). Click the pill in the top-right of the card to filter for dynasties with major events, and click any event to time-travel straight to that year!
  • Strategic Mountain Passes & Poetic / Battlefield Landmarks: Explore famous mountain passes—including , , , , , , and —rendered with traditional gatehouse icons and strategic terrain notes, alongside famous battlefields and literary landmarks such as , , , Orchid Pavilion (Lanting), , , , , , and .

Feature 3: Person Chronicles — Trace Any Historical Figure Across Time & Space

Click the top-left (with a rotatable figure preview and quick-search chips, or type any monarch, general, statesman, monk, or poet such as , , , , or ) to open , marking every milestone of their life with numbered pins across changing dynastic borders:

  • Qin Shi Huang's Unification Campaigns (238–221 BCE): From suppressing the rebellion at Xianyang and Wang Jian's attack on Ye, to the fall of Han, Zhao, Yan, Wei, Chu, and Dai, culminating in the surrender of Qi at Linzi—as you advance stop by stop, watch the six rival kingdoms merge into the Qin Empire right on the map!
  • Zhang Qian's Mission to the Western Regions (138–126 BCE): Depart Chang'an, endure over a decade of Xiongnu captivity without surrendering the Han imperial staff, and blaze the trail to Dayuan (Fergana), Kangju, and the Greater Yuezhi.
  • Zhuge Liang's Emergence & Northern Expeditions (207–234 CE): From the Three Visits at Longzhong and the alliance at Chaisang before Red Cliffs, to entering Shu, the White Emperor City entrustment, the Southern Campaign across the Lu River, Hanzhong's Memorial on Deploying the Troops, Mount Qi, and the autumn winds of Wuzhang Plains.
  • Xuanzang's Pilgrimage to India (627–645 CE): Slip past Yumen Pass alone across the Moheyan Desert, scale the icy Bedel Pass, cross the Indus, study at Nalanda Monastery, and debate at Kanyakubja (Kanauj) before returning to Chang'an.
  • Li Bai's Grand Travels Across Tang China (701–762 CE): From Suyab and boyhood in Shu, sailing out through the Three Gorges at twenty-four, scattering gold in Yangzhou, serving in the Hanlin Academy at Chang'an, meeting Du Fu in Luoyang, receiving amnesty at White Emperor City, to his final years at Dangtu.
  • Su Shi's Literary Exile Across Song China (1056–1101 CE): From leaving Meishan for the capital Kaifeng and gazing at the moon in Mizhou, to composing the in Huangzhou exile, Huizhou, and crossing the sea to Danzhou on Hainan Island.
  • Wang Yangming's Unity of Knowledge & Action (1472–1529 CE): From birth in Yuyao and imprisonment in Beijing, to his enlightenment at Longchang in Guizhou, pacifying bandits in Southern Ganzhou, capturing the rebel Prince of Ning in 35 days, teaching at the Tianquan Bridge in Shaoxing, and his final words "This mind is bright and clear; what more is there to say?" at Nan'an.
  • : Type two or three names into the search box (e.g. or Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan) to merge their journeys onto one timeline. Places where they met in the same year are marked as shared encounters, and the pill narrows the list to just those stops.
  • : Major events unfold stop by stop, just like a person's life. The Chu–Han Contention (207–202 BCE), the An Lushan Rebellion (755–763 CE) and the Jingkang Catastrophe (1125–1142 CE) are each laid out in ten stops across three acts, with the two sides drawn in different colors so each side's advances are easy to follow.

Each time you step to the next event (, , or to auto-play), the timeline year, reigning monarch, imperial era, and dynastic territories evolve in sync with their footsteps, highlighting the active transition arc alongside bilingual primary-source excerpts and poems written at that exact site.

Feature 4: Easter Egg · Map Pinpoint Challenge — What Imperial Court Rank Would You Earn?

Think you know Chinese historical geography? Click in the corner of the guide bar (or type for Map Pinpoint · Ancient Place Quiz):

  • Dynastic Historical Clues + Blind Map Pinpointing: City labels are hidden while the prompt asks you to locate an ancient city across a 10-round progressive difficulty deck—accompanied by dynastic historical clues (without spoiling the modern city name). Drop your pin to preview and adjust, click the chip next to the pin to lock in your answer with concentric distance score rings, and earn points based on great-circle distance to the true coordinates!
  • Complete 10 rounds to receive a traditional imperial cartographic title such as Grand Historian & Master Cartographer (太史令 · 舆图大家), Director of the Bureau of Operations (职方郎中), or Prefectural Retainer (州郡从事).

Keyboard Shortcuts & Shareable Deep Links

Focus the : search (//), (///), (///), (//), poetic & battlefield landmarks (///), (//), , or the
Jump to the previous / next historical phase, milestone event, or person event stop (hold to step by years)

/ Open the 18-era genealogy card for that location
Hover / Click legend swatchHover to isolate & highlight that polity's territory; click to open its profile and zoom to its territory

Append query parameters to share any historical moment, battle, city genealogy, or multi-stop route:

Put any view of the atlas into a blog post, Notion page, or course site:

  1. Open the atlas and set up the view you want (a year, a regime profile, a place card, or a person's trajectory). The address bar always mirrors what you see.
  2. Copy the URL and add .
  3. Paste it into an :
<iframe
  src="https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?embed=1&year=1104&trace=101.778,36.617&from=1072&to=1126&lang=en"
  width="100%" height="480" loading="lazy" style="border:0"
  title="Chronicles of the Realm · 1104 CE, Northern Song"></iframe>

The embedded map hides the site chrome and keeps only the map, a compact timeline, a title chip, an "Open in Jiangshan Atlas ↗" link, and a note that historical borders are approximate. Readers click once to start panning and zooming, so scrolling your page never gets stuck on the map.

Turn on embed mode (required)
, , , , , Same as the share links above
Limit the timeline to this range; the timeline zooms to show only it
Freeze the map at and hide the timeline
Play a person's trajectory stop by stop (with ), or play the timeline

WeChat Official Accounts, Zhihu, and Xiaohongshu do not allow iframes; share the plain link there instead.

AI Agent, MCP & LLM Integration

works out of the box as a historical-geography visualization engine for LLMs, MCP Clients, and AI Agents. Models never need to guess latitude/longitude coordinates—simply extract two semantic parameters from a poem or historical text, and , and the atlas automatically resolves ancient/modern place names, centers the camera, renders dynastic borders and multi-stop trajectories, and opens the genealogy card:

  • Zero-Dependency Local MCP Server (): — add to Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, or Gemini CLI :
    {
  "mcpServers": {
    "jiangshan-atlas": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/jiangshan-map/scripts/mcp_server.js"]
    }
  }
}
    Exposes 3 native MCP tools ( offline response, zero npm dependencies):
    • inspect_place({ year, place, lang? }): Returns reigning monarch/era, controlling regime (), macro-region (), prefecture (), modern province/city, 2,400-year , and shareable deep-link URL.
    • inspect_person({ person, stop?, lang? }): Returns a historical figure or monarch's biography, chronological geocoded stops across dynasties, and shareable deep-link URL.
    • search_atlas({ query, limit?, lang? }): Searches across all ancient cities, poetic & battlefield landmarks, mountain passes, historical figures, imperial eras, and chronological milestones.

1. Zero-Coordinate Dual-Parameter URL Protocol (0D Pinpoint / 1D Same-Year Route / 4D Multi-Year Route)

Automatic Rendering Behavior
Single-Point Pinpoint (0D)Jumps to Tang Yuanhe 14 (819 CE), drops a pin on Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains, and opens its 2,400-year administrative genealogy card
Same-Year Multi-Stop Route (1D)Plots numbered vermilion arcs → across the 763 CE Tang map and auto-fits the viewport; click any stop to inspect its genealogy
Multi-Year Space-Time Route (4D)Pairs with , labeling stops with their historical years and switching the underlying dynastic map whenever you click a stop

2. CLI One-Command Screenshot & JSON Lookup (for Agent Tool Calls)

# Single-point poetic landmark screenshot
python3 skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py --year 819 --place 蓝关 --out /tmp/languan_819.png

# Same-year multi-stop trajectory screenshot
python3 skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py --year 763 --place 剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳 --out /tmp/dufu_763.png

# Multi-year space-time trajectory screenshot
python3 skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py --year 1079,1080,1094,1097 --place 湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州 --out /tmp/sushi_exile.png

3. Browser JavaScript API () & In-Browser WebMCP ()

In browser automation environments (Playwright) or WebMCP-enabled AI browsers (), the page automatically registers , , and , and exposes :

  • window.atlasAPI.locate({ year, place, zoom? }): Drives the map to a single location or multi-stop trajectory and returns structured historical-geographic metadata.
  • window.atlasAPI.inspect({ year, place, person?, stop? }): Read-only query returning the controlling polity, ancient prefecture, modern province/city, leg distances, person events, and canonical shareable URL.
  • window.atlasAPI.resolvePlace(place, year?): Resolves ancient and modern names for cities, strategic passes, poetic landmarks, and battlefields.
  • window.atlasAPI.openPerson(person, stop?) & window.atlasAPI.search(query): Opens a person chronicle on the map or searches across the entire atlas.

No dependencies or build steps required. Clone and serve with any static HTTP server:

git clone https://github.com/DeanChensj/jiangshan-map.git
cd jiangshan-map
python3 -m http.server 8000

Then open in your browser.

No local dependency needed. Build and start with Docker Compose:

docker compose up -d --build

Then open (the port mapping is set in ).

The image is a plain that serves this repository as static files: copies the working tree into , and keeps the build context small by excluding , , , , , , , Markdown files, and the README demo images (, ) — the site does not need any of them at runtime.

To use another port, change the mapping in (e.g. ) and run again.

After pulling upstream changes, rebuild with docker compose up -d --build. Without Compose: docker build -t jiangshan-map:latest . then docker run -d -p 8008:80 --name jiangshan-map jiangshan-map:latest.

Note: the image is built locally; it is not published to any registry.

GeoJSON Export (for Leaflet / MapLibre / QGIS)

The app ships its geometry as compact topology-deduplicated VLQ bundles. To use the vector layers in other projects, generate standard RFC 7946 GeoJSON (EPSG:4326, lon/lat) locally; the output goes to and is not committed. The export covers 403 BCE to 1948; later years and the modern province layer are not included. The prefecture layer (郡 / 州 / 府) is left out by default because it derives from CHGIS, whose terms forbid redistribution; add to include it for local academic, non-commercial use, and do not publish the result.

node scripts/export_geojson.js            # or: node scripts/export_geojson.js <outDir>
node scripts/export_geojson.js --with-prefectures   # adds the CHGIS-derived prefecture layer (local academic use only)
  • — one file per territorial phase; each feature has a and ( / , plus with ), , , , , .
  • — every dynasty's phases with / years (negative = BCE, no year 0) and the matching snapshot file.
  • (walls, canals, roads, sea routes), , , , and (rivers, lakes, hydro labels; / give the years historical river courses and lakes are shown).

To look up a point without loading every phase, use geojson/jiangshan-locate.js: it loads plus only the snapshot covering the year, then runs a bbox-filtered point-in-polygon test.

const atlas = JiangshanLocate.create(); // or create({ base: '<url of geojson/>' })
const hit = await atlas.locate(118.78, 32.06, 1415); // lon, lat, year
hit.polity.properties.title;     // 明
hit.region.properties.title;     // 南直隶
hit.prefecture;                  // null unless exported with --with-prefectures (then 应天府)

After exporting, serve the repository (python3 -m http.server 8000) and open http://localhost:8000/geojson/demo.html for a Leaflet example: drag the year slider, click the map, or open demo.html?year=1415&lon=118.78&lat=32.06 to load, highlight and zoom automatically. Historical borders are schematic approximations, not surveyed boundaries. The data is GPL-3.0 except the prefecture-level boundaries; see Data Sources & License.

Code and the data created by this project are released under . One layer is not: the prefecture-level boundaries derived from CHGIS, which stay under CHGIS's own terms.

Code (app, scripts, CLI, MCP server)
First-level divisions (: 刺史部 / 道 / 路 / 省 …)Drawn by hand from historical texts; the source of early versions was not recorded
Prefecture-level boundaries (: 郡 / 州 / 府, incl. Warring States and Qin commanderies)Derived from and the Robert M. Hartwell China Historical GIS, simplified to 0.01° and edited by hand Academic, non-commercial use only; do not redistribute. See below
Settlements, milestones, journeys, person chronicles, place loreCompiled by this project from historical texts
DataV GeoAtlas (Alibaba Cloud)Subject to DataV GeoAtlas terms
Rivers, lakes, neighbouring countries
Rendered by scripts/build_terrain_tiles.py from AWS Terrain Tiles (public-domain , , ); only shaded images at no finer than about 1 km per pixel are published
Wikimedia Commons (, , , , )

Scholarly references (not data sources). Boundaries are checked against historical texts and Tan Qixiang's The Historical Atlas of China (谭其骧主编《中国历史地图集》). No map images or data from that atlas are included in this repository.

Prefecture-level boundaries (CHGIS). This layer is not covered by GPL-3.0 and is shown here for non-commercial, educational use. Do not republish it from this repository; if you need prefecture boundaries, download CHGIS from its official distribution (Harvard Dataverse) under its terms. scripts/export_geojson.js leaves this layer out unless run with . Cite it as: CHGIS, Version: 6. © Fairbank Center for Chinese Studies of Harvard University and the Center for Historical Geographical Studies at Fudan University, 2016. Provenance details: data/atlas/README.md.

Historical territories and administrative boundaries are schematic approximations of broad jurisdictions, not surveyed borders. Do not cite them as precise or authoritative.

For the GPL-3.0 layers, credit with a link to https://github.com/DeanChensj/jiangshan-map and cite the upstream sources above. Screenshots that show the prefecture layer carry the CHGIS terms as well.

If you hold rights in any material here and believe it is used improperly, please open an issue; we will respond and remove it if needed.

items.title: NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator
items.content:
Multi-tier framework for evaluating AI agent skills and plugins with quality gates, security scanning, harness compatibility checks, semantic overlap detection, synthetic evaluation dataset generation, and live agent evaluation that measures how skills affect agent behavior. Ships reusable CI templates that bring every check to any repository.

SkillEvaluator checks AI agent skills and plugins, and measures a skill's effect on task results: start with quality checks, then compare runs with and without a skill.

Catch skill issues before merge. Connect your repository to SkillEvaluator with a CI template for automated quality and security gates, without building or maintaining evaluation code.

Install the CLI in a Python 3.12–3.14 environment:

pip install skillevaluator

For uv setup or direct GitHub source installation, see Installation.

Then check skills from your terminal, CI, or agent:

Run checks backed by 500+ static rules and detection patterns, without an LLM key. Complete scanner setup for full coverage:

skillevaluator validate \
  ./my-skill --tiers 1

Add the skill to Claude Code, Codex or another agent:

Chart is self-hosted — regenerate with python3 scripts/gen_star_history.py (needs ). Refreshes automatically each day via .github/workflows/star-history.yml.

Scope — what this bundle is for, and what it isn't

This bundle covers the — anything reachable from the internet without first compromising an internal endpoint.

  • — web apps, APIs, SaaS, GraphQL, OAuth, JWT, file upload, IDOR, SSRF, RCE chains
  • Web application pentesting — full hunt-* coverage of OWASP-mapped bug classes + discipline rules
  • External red-team engagements — initial-access against internet-facing enterprise estate: M365 / Entra ID, Okta-as-IdP, SharePoint on-prem (ToolShell + legacy SOAP), VMware vCenter / Workspace ONE, SSL VPN appliances (Cisco / Fortinet / Citrix / Palo Alto / Pulse / SonicWall / F5), Android APK red-team, supply-chain recon

  • — H1, Bugcrowd (VRT-aware), Intigriti, Immunefi, plus client-facing red-team deliverable format

Out of scope (deliberate — not gaps, design decisions)

  • Internal Active Directory attacks — BloodHound, Kerberoasting, ASREProast, DCSync, Pass-the-Hash, AD CS abuse, ntlmrelayx, Responder, PetitPotam, etc. Different operational risk profile; needs different tooling and judgment. Future bundle, not this one.
  • — Cobalt Strike, Sliver, Mythic, Havoc, BRC4 tradecraft. Out of scope for external-only engagement model.
  • Post-exploit / persistence / lateral — Mimikatz/comsvcs LSASS dumping, golden/silver tickets, named-pipe impersonation, persistence (registry, scheduled tasks, WMI events, COM hijacking), token theft. These start after the perimeter has already broken — different bundle territory.
  • — AMSI bypass, ETW patching, AV/EDR bypass. Tied to C2 tradecraft above.
  • iOS pentesting / hardware / RF / ICS — out of scope by design.
  • Binary exploitation / kernel pwn / browser internals — different skill universe.

If you're running an internal red team that includes domain-takeover chains via Kerberos or lateral movement, this bundle won't help you in those phases — and we'd rather say that up front than have you find out mid-engagement. The external surface handoff to internal-RT tooling (Impacket, NetExec, CrackMapExec, Rubeus, Certify, BloodHound) is intentionally outside our scope. Coverage for internal AD and post-exploit may come in a future update.

The skills include validation gates that auto-trigger when you point Claude at unverified third-party targets — 's 7-Question Gate explicitly asks whether the asset is in scope (Q3) and on the program's accepted-impact list (Q2). The bundle explicitly : weaponizing 0-days against unauthorized targets, post-exploitation tooling, malware development, mass-targeting infrastructure. See for the full posture.

Heads-up — Anthropic runtime cyber safeguards. Anthropic's models apply real-time safeguards that block "vulnerability exploitation or offensive security tooling development" by default — so even work can hit a refusal that isn't this bundle's doing. If you do authorized offensive security (pentest / bug bounty / red team), enroll in Anthropic's to get safeguards adjusted for legitimate dual-use work. (Mass data exfiltration and ransomware development stay prohibited and are adjustable.) Details: Anthropic — real-time cyber safeguards.

Why your model switched mid-session

Separate from refusals, and easy to miss. On , a narrow set of higher-risk cyber requests — Anthropic names , binary-based vulnerability scanning and — rather than being refused. You get a notice and the response is labelled with the model that answered, but in a long agentic run that is easy to scroll past, so it can look like Opus 5 quietly got worse. See why Claude switched models.

What to do depends on what you are actually doing:

— reviewing a repo you own for defectsSay so. "Defensive review of my own repo", "check this against the OWASP Top 10", "secure refactor to remediate" describe the work accurately and read as remediation. This is not a workaround; the work genuinely is defensive.
Authorized offensive work — live engagement, PoC for a bounty submissionThis is what the bundle is for, and the supported route is CVP. Do not reword an offensive engagement to look defensive to get past a classifier — enroll instead.
You just want the switching offSettings → Capabilities disables automatic model switching.

  5. No post-credential escalation model — when recon yielded credentials (AWS keys, JWTs, GCP JSON), it was unclear what they granted or how to escalate →

The per-class skills address gap-zero ("what should I look for in webapps") — the original 24 codifying patterns from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports, with 20+ framework/surface skills added by the community v3 expansion — Claude knows the actual chain templates real triagers paid for, not abstract OWASP Top 10. Tensor library for machine learning

git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml
cd ggml

mkdir build && cd build
cmake ..
cmake --build . --config Release -j 8

For a minimal, fully commented example (matrix multiplication), see examples/simple.

The main goal of is to be a simple, portable, and efficient tensor library for machine learning with minimal setup.

  • Plain C/C++ implementation without any dependencies
  • Cross-platform - x86, ARM, RISC-V, LoongArch, PowerPC, s390x, and WebAssembly
  • SIMD-optimized kernels for x86, ARM, and RISC-V
  • Broad backend support - CPU, GPU, NPU, and browser

  • For changes to the core library (including to the CMake build system), please open a PR in llama.cpp - doing so will make your PR more visible, better tested, and more likely to be reviewed

{

items.title: Tencent/LoopForge
items.content:
Self-hosted workflows for coding-agent delivery. Orchestrate CodeBuddy, Codex and Claude Code with scripts and human approval gates. Includes Local workflows for coding assistants.

80-second product tour (1080p, with sound).

is a self-hosted workspace where your team ships software with coding agents. Describe what you need to in chat: it opens a Docker sandbox, checks out your repositories, delegates to project roles, and opens the PR. When a way of working proves itself, save it as an (a standard workflow of agents, scripts and human gates) so the next requirement is delivered the same way, with review and approval built in.

Coding-agent CLIs do the work: CodeBuddy, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Antigravity, Kimi Code, Pi, DeepSeek Harness and ZCode. LoopForge adds the roles, sandboxes, checkpoints and history around them, all on your own infrastructure under the MIT license.

Exploring, quick fixes, iterating with the agentRepeatable delivery with fixed stages and sign-off
Main Bot opens a conversation workspace (a Docker sandbox with your repos) on demand and calls project roles as subagentsThe engine runs Agent, Script, Human-gate and sub-SOP nodes in order, in their own sandbox
Queuing or steering messages mid-reply, and pausing, resuming or taking over a running SOP from chatApproving at human gates, sending work back to a chosen step, retrying or rerunning from any node
A PR/MR, or a direct merge into a shared branch ()Documents, code or a PR, plus per-node artifacts and logs

Both paths track the same , so every change, whether made in chat or by an SOP, links back to what was asked for and counts toward delivery and cost reports.

The chat home. Type a request, a role, skill, requirement, SOP or repository, and pick the executor, model and permission mode per conversation.

Ask a coding agent to "fix this bug" and the result depends on that run. It might skip the plan, forget the tests, review its own code, or stop halfway without anyone noticing. That's fine for a demo, but it isn't how a team ships.

  • Same SOP, same stages, same checks for every requirement. Start from built-in backend, frontend, bug-fix and product SOPs.
  • Planning, implementation, review and testing each get their own prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills and MCP tools. A role works as an SOP node or as a subagent in chat.
  • Approval gates where they matter. Read the report, approve, or send the work back to a chosen step.
  • Observable and resumable. Node status, tool traces, logs and artifacts in one place. Pause, retry a failed step, or rerun from any node.
  • Your stack, your servers. Ten coding-agent CLIs as executors, from CodeBuddy, Codex and Claude Code to OpenCode, Cursor CLI and more. GitHub, Skills and MCP as tools. Docker sandboxes or your own machine as the runtime.

Install and clone the repository first. The installer checks Docker, Compose, Python 3 and curl and offers to install missing components. Python/curl installation supports apt, dnf and yum on Linux; the Compose plugin supports x86_64/arm64 and verifies the official release SHA-256. macOS needs a working Python 3 and Docker Desktop; Homebrew can install missing components. Ordinary Linux users are supported through Docker group access or sudo. Set to accept installation prompts. Package and image downloads require internet access.

git clone https://github.com/Tencent/LoopForge.git
cd LoopForge
./start.sh

pulls the GHCR release image pinned in without building locally ( does the same). It creates the MySQL and platform services, generates configuration and session secrets, and installs the built-in sandboxes, starter SOPs and welcome project. Host Go and Node.js installations are not required. Configure model API keys and GitHub authorization after startup. Use , , or to manage it, and to build the checkout from source.

If downloads from stall, set to a registry host that can stand in for . pulls from that host and tags the image back to the name pinned in . Setting trusts that host, because the download is tagged with the official name. The GitHub Release records the digest; docker image inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' ghcr.io/tencent/loopforge:<pin> should show the same digest after . Without , still pulls directly, and stays unchanged. Upgrade with the same variable and . ghcr.nju.edu.cn is one such host. A Docker entry such as https://docker.nju.edu.cn only accelerates Docker Hub and is not a value for .

MIRROR=ghcr.nju.edu.cn ./start.sh

Open the address printed by the installer and create your account; the first one becomes the administrator. The service listens on by default. On a cloud host, the installer reads the public IP from the provider's metadata service and prints it; allow the port in your security group, or put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front. Restrict access to your own IP until the administrator account exists. The home page's quick-access guide walks you through adding a model key, connecting a repository and choosing an SOP.

For GitLab, Gitea, Gogs and other Git hosts, set up Git SSH to check out and push branches with a personal key. PR/MR and Issue automation requires a hosting API token or a separately configured MCP.

Try it without an API key

New accounts join the , which includes an SOP made only of a script and a human gate:

  1. Switch to the demo project, open , and open Platform check · script & approval.
  2. Click . A real script writes a report, then the run waits for you at the approval step.
  3. Approve it from or the run page, and watch the run continue to its final artifact.

What you need for real work

Run the script + approval demo
Chat with Main Bot, generate a document or a new projectAn API key for the selected executor
Change an existing repository (in chat or via an SOP) and open a PRModel credentials and a GitHub repository (connect GitHub in personal settings)

An is the workflow a delivery follows. Agents, scripts and people take part in the same run:

The SOP designer with the built-in bug-fix SOP. Each step picks a role; failed checks can send the work back to an earlier step.

A role (prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills and MCP tools) that designs, implements, reviews or tests.
A deterministic shell step: build, test, lint, generate a report. No AI where AI is not needed.
Pauses the run until someone checks the artifacts and approves, or sends the work back to a step.
Runs another SOP as a sub-workflow.
Builds a static site and archives it for review.

Each node declares its artifacts and dependencies, and the engine starts each step once its dependencies complete. Start from a built-in SOP, adapt its roles, rules and environment to your project, and publish versions as it evolves.

A run waiting at a human gate: approve and continue, add context and rerun the step, or send the work back upstream.

A delivery we actually ran: four CodeBuddy roles planned a Python fix, implemented it, reviewed it independently and summarized the delivery. Three real tests passed; the run waited for human approval, then verified the accepted code had not changed. The reusable acceptance case checks the files and results. See the validation record for scope and known gaps.

Main Bot with per-conversation executor, model and permission mode. references for roles, skills, requirements, SOPs and repositories. Messages queue while a reply runs; interrupts and sends now. Generated files open in a side panel with preview, source and download.
On-demand Docker sandboxes with the project's repositories checked out, project roles as native subagents, and direct control of a running SOP workspace: pause, resume or take over.
Visual canvas with Agent, Script, Human gate, Sub-SOP and Preview nodes, rework-on-failure edges, validation, version history and publishing. Built-in backend, frontend, bug-fix and product SOPs.
Reusable definitions: prompt, executor, model, rules, Skills, MCP tools, artifacts and gates, shared across SOP nodes and chat subagents.
Requirements tracked end to end, whether shipped by an SOP or straight from chat, with PR/MR status tracking, merge detection and direct-branch merges.
Live node status, tool traces, worker logs, per-node artifact snapshots and workspace previews. A single inbox for every gate waiting on you.
Recurring agent tasks with full workspace, SOP and MCP access; a shared market of versioned, parameterized task templates; automatic SOP dispatch for new requirements.
Engineering metrics, business-domain reports with static HTML/SVG export, and token/cost accounting for SOPs and conversations at public list prices.
Platform workers, Docker sandboxes, or a connected local execution machine using your own tools and repositories.
Password accounts, projects and members, light/dark/system themes, an OpenAPI-described HTTP and MCP API. Management pages are in English and Chinese; the chat workbench is Chinese for now.

Built-in SOPs are read-only blueprints; copy one into your project to run and edit it.

Don't want to run a server? brings the built-in delivery workflows straight into the coding assistant you already use:

# Run inside your target project, e.g. for Claude Code
npx -y loopforge-cli@latest install claude

Then run /start-devflow "<your request>" in Claude Code.

Claude Code · CodeBuddy · Codex · CursorClassic (default) and Portable editions

See the local guide for each host's entry point and editions for the differences. Source lives in . Local runs the built-in workflows today; exporting a platform SOP for standalone local execution is planned.

Teams sharing chat workspaces, SOPs, approvals and historyOne developer inside an IDE or CLI
Node.js 20+, Python 3.8+ and a coding assistant
Chat with Main Bot + custom SOPs on a visual canvasBuilt-in Classic / Portable workflows
Shared run details, approvals and metrics in the web workspaceArtifacts under + optional local dashboard

Do I need an API key to try it? No. The demo SOP uses only a script and a human gate. Chat and agent steps need a key for the executor you pick. Model usage is not included; you bring your own credentials.

No. Chat, documents and new projects run in the task workspace. Connect GitHub when you want to change an existing repository or open PRs.

Should I use chat or an SOP? Use chat to explore and iterate; Main Bot can still open a PR. Once you find a way of working you want every requirement to follow, with fixed reviewers, tests and sign-off, put it in an SOP. Main Bot can start, pause and take over SOP runs, so the two paths work together.

How is this different from Dify, n8n or Flowise? Those are general-purpose AI and automation workflow builders. LoopForge is built for software delivery with coding agents: implementer and reviewer roles, Docker sandboxes with real repositories, GitHub delivery, human acceptance gates and run evidence.

How is this different from using Claude Code, Codex, CodeBuddy or another coding CLI directly? LoopForge doesn't replace them; it orchestrates them. Each agent step and each chat turn runs one of those CLIs. LoopForge adds what surrounds it: who does what, in which sandbox, in which order, with which checks, and who signs off.

Is it safe to expose on the internet? New installations listen on all interfaces and target a trusted team. Read the account and access model and set up HTTPS before opening it up. Report vulnerabilities privately via the security policy.

Scan the QR code to join the LoopForge community group.

Issues and PRs are welcome: share a use case, report a bug, or improve workflows, integrations and the platform experience. Start with the contributing guide. Security issues go through the security policy.

If LoopForge is useful to you, a star helps others find it.

🪨 why use many token when few token do trick. Viral skill + proxy for coding agents that cuts 65% of tokens by talking like a caveman.

The reason your React component is re-rendering is likely because you're creating a new object reference on each render cycle. When you pass an inline object as a prop, React's shallow comparison sees it as a different object every time, which triggers a re-render. I'd recommend using useMemo to memoize the object.

New object ref each render, so React re-renders. Wrap the prop in .

Same fix. 63 token become 20. Brain still big.

New object ref each render, so React re-renders. Wrap the prop in .
Inline object prop, new ref, re-render. .

Token counts: tiktoken o200k.

npx @caveman-ai/cli@latest

One command. Mac, Linux, Windows. Caveman find your agents and your logins, show what it change. Press Enter. Done. Needs Node.js 22.13+.

After that, plain stays caveman'd. So do Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and 30+ more. It runs on your machine, with your keys and your Claude Pro/Max login. One rock. That it.

Had caveman before 4.0? Say , or the old copy on your machine wins. Already set up? opens the screen again. Only want shorter answers? Get just the skill.

New in 4.0: caveman is six parts. All on after install. Each has its own switch.

Agent answers short. Code stays exact
Logs, JSON, CSV, test output shrink before the model reads them fewer input tokens per session
Picks the model and the effort for each ask cheaper than Opus at xhigh, same score
Code mode: agent keeps the scripts it writes and runs them again tokens for one test run
Finds where your tokens go and fixes it. New: keeps the prompt cache warm while you pause
Web pages come back compressed

shows what is on. turns one off. Only Auto needs an account, and it is free. 4.0.0 release notes

Outside labs first. Ours come with each rock below. Nothing rounded up. Red rows stay red.

Caveman-style output, eight models, five datasetsCost cut 1.4 to 2.4× per model, up to 3×
Caveman mode remade for Elasticsearch, eight live MCP scenarios63.6% fewer response tokens.
86 real coding tasks, paired A/BNo measurable quality loss (p = 0.82). 8.5% fewer output tokens

Two findings shaped caveman. Adobe: cavemanning prompt makes answers worse, so caveman never touches your prompt. JetBrains: agent sessions are mostly code and tool calls, which the voice leaves alone. So caveman grew rocks that shrink what the agent and what it .

Say less: the caveman voice

A voice, not broken grammar. Every reply follows the same structure.

[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step]. No greeting, no "let me", no recap
Built on ASD-STE100, the controlled English of aircraft maintenance manuals: 20 words max, active voice, one term per thing
Articles can go. , , , never go. Numbers and units stay exact
Code, commands, paths, and error messages untouched, character for character
No "me think". No chatter between tool calls. If caveman phrasing isn't shorter, plain wins
Security warnings, irreversible actions, and confused users get full sentences. Then grunt resumes

Ten dev questions on claude-opus-5-5:

"Be concise" is the real baseline; new models already know it. On top of it, cuts 3% more at the median and 35% more. Measured on the 3.1.0 rules, not yet re-run. The rules cost about 1,160 tokens of input, and if you pay per request (GitHub Copilot), shorter answers save nothing. Harness · Every case where caveman loses

The skill alone, no proxy:

npx skills add JuliusBrussee/caveman -g

Type ( in Codex) if it doesn't start on its own. Say to go back.

Read less: 33.2% fewer input tokens

The voice shrinks what the agent says. This shrinks what it reads. Same answers: 18 of 18 right.

The file, through cavemanWhole Claude Code session, 3 runs

is each test file through today's compressor alone. is the whole agent run, which also carries the system prompt and tools, so it moves less. Honest part: the session run is from August 2026 on an older engine, HTML has no compressor yet so it lost, and each test file hides one record in 61 to 72 KB of noise. Yours will vary. Headroom on the same suite: 15 of 18 right, 6.7% fewer tokens. Method

Every original stays on your disk. The agent can pull it back any time.

Auto: 54% cheaper, same score

New model in your agent's picker. Pick Auto and caveman chooses the model and the effort for each ask. Hard ask, big brain. Easy ask, save rocks.

Opus 5.5, xhigh effort, every ask

Auto costs 0.46× what Opus 5.5 at xhigh costs. That is 54% saved, in under half the time. 85 real coding tasks from SWE-Interact and SWE-Together, one try each. Honest part: the run is half done, the 0.5-point score gap is too small to tell apart at this size (±7), and most of the saving is Auto lowering effort on easy asks. Already on Opus at medium? Expect less; not measured yet. Full table and limits

Works in Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex on a ChatGPT login, with API keys, Claude Pro/Max, or ChatGPT. Any other model you pick runs as picked. Not signed in: no Auto, nothing sent. What Auto sends

, 326 tests

Tokens the agent reads back. In one week, agents on one machine wrote the same script 394 times. Purdue measured the habit at up to 9.57% of task cost. loses to a bare grep; row stays. Method

Comes with caveman. Eight blocks ready: · · · · · · · . When the agent starts typing a script a block already covers, it gets one line: use the block. Never denies or rewrites a command.

Subagents that find, edit, and review code, then report back in caveman

Everything above is for the coding agent you use. Caveman Cloud is for the agents you build.

You ship an agent. Every run costs money. Is it good? Is it cheap? Which change made it worse? Cloud answers.

items.title: ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui
items.content:
AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.

AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.

Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent. The same agent can power a web app, a mobile app, a terminal, or Slack.

The protocol now has a stable, frozen specification backed by a JSON Schema, and the TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs are generated from it. 1.0 is backwards compatible in both directions: 0.x agents work with 1.0 clients and vice versa. What changed → · Migration guide →

The CLI scaffolds a frontend (CopilotKit on Next.js, or a terminal client) wired to the agent framework you pick:

npx create-ag-ui-app@latest

Then follow the printed next steps. The generated templates call OpenAI, so set your key before :

export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."

AG-UI is one of three open, complementary agentic protocols. gives agents tools and context, lets agents work with other agents, and brings agents to users. A single agent often uses all three, and AG-UI can front agents that speak MCP or A2A. Read more →

They work together. A2UI, MCP Apps, and Open-JSON-UI are : they describe what UI an agent wants to show. AG-UI is the that carries those payloads, along with everything else, between the agent and the app. Learn more →

AG-UI is adopted by Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle, and built into most agent frameworks. Every framework below has a live demo in the Dojo.

Full list of integrations

Features: what you can build

Each building block maps to events in the spec, and each has a live demo in the AG-UI Dojo.

Token-by-token messages across multi-turn sessions, with cancel and resume
Agents render typed components, or declarative UI with A2UI and MCP Apps
A typed store the agent and app both read and write, synced with snapshots and JSON Patch deltas
The agent calls tools that run in the app, and gets the result back
Runs end with an outcome; the user approves, edits, or rejects, and the next run resumes
Show the agent's reasoning as it works, including encrypted reasoning round-trips
Nested delegation, with every event attributed to the subagent run that produced it
Images, audio, video, and documents in user input and tool results

Tool output streaming, backend tool rendering, activity progress, token usage, and custom events are covered in the docs. Here's a quick tour of the Dojo:

Your app starts a run by sending the agent a single : the conversation, the tools the frontend offers, shared state, and context. The agent answers with a stream of typed events from eight families: run lifecycle, text messages, tool calls, state, reasoning, activity, subagents, and custom events (full list). Only the run lifecycle is required, so a minimal agent emits a handful of events and grows from there.

AG-UI 1.0 defines 31 event types in eight families. See the spec for every field.

(JSON Patch)
REASONING_ENCRYPTED_VALUE

AG-UI was created by CopilotKit and is developed in the open with the community.

items.title: dream-num/univer
items.content:
Build your own AI office with Univer Office SDK. Bring editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing into your product for people and AI agents. Built on an extensible open-source core.

Start with open-source Sheets and Docs, then connect your own application or agent.

is an Office SDK for building Office applications inside your own product. It provides Office editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing for people and existing agents, using your data and permissions. The product family covers spreadsheets, documents, presentations, relational tables, canvases, and PDFs.

Univer Office SDK has three parts:

  • is the foundation: content models, editing, rendering, formula calculation, and Facade APIs (application-facing APIs). Compose its plugins into an embedded editor or your own Office application, and reuse the content models, commands, and calculation for Headless processing without an interactive editor.
  • adds backend services for real-time collaboration, edit history, and Office file import and export.
  • connects Office capabilities to existing agents and workflows, with content tools, execution, and review integrations.

This repository provides the Web SDK's core architecture and engine implementations under Apache-2.0: content models and snapshot formats, plugin and dependency management, the command system, formula and rendering engines, Facade APIs, UI foundation, and Sheets and Docs editing capabilities. Commercial Web SDK plugins, Server SDK, and commercial AI SDK extensions are distributed and licensed separately.

Agents can use the same open-source APIs; your application supplies the model and tool orchestration. The quotation example demonstrates editing, calculation, and saving without an AI SDK dependency.

Sheets · Editing and layoutCell styles, merged cells, in-cell rich text, freeze panes, floating images, and undo/redo.
Sheets · Data and calculationFormulas, defined names, filtering, sorting, data validation, conditional formatting, hyperlinks, comments, and find and replace.
Rich-text editing, paragraph formatting, lists, hyperlinks, comments, and drawing integration.

Features are composed through plugins and presets; the quick start uses only the . Images use the corresponding drawing plugins. See the feature comparison for detailed open-source and commercial coverage.

The demos below showcase the wider , including commercial capabilities. They show more than the default open-source setup; see open source and commercial extensions for scope.

🚀 Build on the open-source foundation

Use the open-source foundation
Add an editable Office surface to your application or agent product, and connect your data through Facade APIs.
Process content without an editorReuse content plugins, models, commands, and calculation in Node.js for editing, snapshots, and automated tasks.
Develop custom features or editorsReuse the engines, UI components, plugin boundaries, dependency injection, and command/undo systems. Follow existing features to extend Sheets and Docs or develop your own editors.

Coordinate edits and undo/redo across features. Inserting a row inside a filter range changes both the base content and the filter range; undo needs to restore both. Each feature supplies its own changes and undo data, and the command composes their execution and history. The architecture walkthrough explains how to extend these editing workflows.

Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor

In a browser application using a bundler such as Vite:

pnpm add @univerjs/presets @univerjs/preset-sheets-core

Create the container before initializing Univer:

<div id="app" style="height: 100vh"></div>

import { UniverSheetsCorePreset } from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core'
import UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/locales/en-US'
import { createUniver, LocaleType, mergeLocales } from '@univerjs/presets'
import '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/lib/index.css'

const { univerAPI } = createUniver({
  locale: LocaleType.EN_US,
  locales: {
    [LocaleType.EN_US]: mergeLocales(UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS),
  },
  presets: [
    UniverSheetsCorePreset({
      container: 'app',
    }),
  ],
})

univerAPI.createWorkbook({})

Your page now contains a spreadsheet editor. Use the returned to work with its content. This example uses open-source packages and needs no commercial Univer license or Server SDK.

For component frameworks, retain the instance returned by and call when the component unmounts. See the lifecycle guide.

Presets compose plugins and register their Facade APIs. For manual control, see the Plugin Mode example below. The installation guide covers both modes, peer dependencies, and framework integrations.

Keep coordinated packages on the same version. Commercial packages must use the matching release line; independently released packages such as icons follow their declared compatibility. See the API Stability Policy.

Connect your application to editable content

Facade APIs are the application-facing interface to workbooks, worksheets, and ranges. Continue from the quick start to populate a quotation, update a quantity from application code, and read the recalculated total:

// Wait for formula controllers before editing a newly created workbook.
await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
  if (univerAPI.getCurrentLifecycleStage() >= univerAPI.Enum.LifecycleStages.Steady) {
    resolve()
    return
  }
  const listener = univerAPI.addEvent(univerAPI.Event.LifeCycleChanged, ({ stage }) => {
    if (stage === univerAPI.Enum.LifecycleStages.Steady) {
      listener.dispose()
      resolve()
    }
  })
})

const workbook = univerAPI.getActiveWorkbook()!
const sheet = workbook.getActiveSheet()

sheet.getRange('A1:D4').setValues([
  ['Item', 'Quantity', 'Unit price', 'Amount'],
  ['Seats', 2, 25, '=B2*C2'],
  ['Support', 1, 100, '=B3*C3'],
  ['Total', '', '', '=SUM(D2:D3)'],
])

// An application control or agent can make the same edit.
sheet.getRange('B2').setValue(4)

univerAPI.getFormula().onCalculationResultApplied().then(() => {
  console.log(sheet.getRange('D4').getValue()) // 200
  localStorage.setItem('quotation', JSON.stringify(workbook.save()))
}).catch(console.error)

The editor and your application operate on the same workbook; formula changes are recalculated automatically. returns a JSON snapshot containing the workbook and its registered plugin data. Your application owns persistence; this example uses browser storage. On a later page load, after initialization, restore the snapshot instead of creating a blank workbook:

const saved = localStorage.getItem('quotation')
if (saved) {
  univerAPI.createWorkbook(JSON.parse(saved))
}

This workflow uses only open-source packages. Snapshot persistence is separate from XLSX import and export, which uses the separately distributed file-conversion capabilities. Use public Facade APIs for application integration; the source links below explain internal implementation and extension points. See the API Stability Policy before depending on an extension point.

🏗️ Explore the open-source architecture

Give custom features clear boundaries

Univer organizes content logic and UI interaction in separate plugins. Feature plugins manage rules and content changes; UI plugins provide the interface and user interactions. For example, manages filter ranges and rules, while provides panels, menus, and shortcuts.

%%{init: {'htmlLabels': false, 'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Arial, PingFang SC, Microsoft YaHei, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '17px', 'lineColor': '#64748b'}, 'flowchart': {'htmlLabels': false, 'curve': 'linear', 'nodeSpacing': 28, 'rankSpacing': 45, 'padding': 16, 'wrappingWidth': 270}}}%%
%% A layered overview, not a complete dependency graph.
%% Group arrows indicate reuse of the layer below; internal arrows show selected dependencies.
flowchart TD
  subgraph FEATURES["Feature Plugins"]
    direction LR
    FUI["Filter<br/>UI Plugin"]

  end

  subgraph FOUNDATION["Core Framework & Plugins"]
